title: Teodoro says businesses should strengthen supply chain resilience amid China concerns
summary: Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. on Tuesday said businesses in the Philippines should strengthen their supply chain resilience following concerns with their existing trade ties with China amid…

blocks.text: Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. on Tuesday said businesses in the Philippines should strengthen their supply chain resilience following concerns with their existing trade ties with China amid the tension in the West Philippine Sea (WPS).

At a press conference, Teodoro was asked about reports that some businesses were concerned that the Philippines' firm stance on the WPS could affect imports, exports and supply chains involving China.
“It behooves businesses, particularly those who perform a function which is vested with public interest, a critical service to make their supply chains more resilient,” he said.
Teodoro cited the COVID-19 pandemic as an example of the importance of preparing for supply chain disruptions.

“The pandemic proved that if you don't invest in the technology, you'll be at the last of the line when the vaccines came out. So, I think, I understand that businesses have comfortable supply chains with China, but it is a responsible thing to be resilient,” he added.
Asked whether business leaders had raised concerns with him about his position on China, Teodoro said none had directly approached him.
“Now, if the businesses feel one way or the other towards me, then they can tell me or they can announce it if they want to. I don't mind,” Teodoro said.

Earlier, several business and civil society groups have called on Philippine and Chinese officials to exercise sobriety and restraint and renew diplomatic engagement amid recent heated public exchanges between government officials and the Chinese Embassy.
In a joint statement, the groups warned against the dangers of public recriminations and inflammatory rhetoric, urging both sides to return to established diplomatic channels. — BAP, GMA News
